attrs.description: Every number a post or an account can earn, per platform: what it is, the API and scope behind it, whether we read it, and the one step that would let us
The week's "what worked": per platform and for all of them, the best and worst post, the number that moved most against the week before, what to make next, and cadence against the goals
His posting plan as a setting (`marketing.cadence`): the goals Plan, the digest and Today measure against

Analytics as console records: how conversations go (`marketing.conversation`), the week's digest (`marketing.digest`), cadence against goals (`marketing.cadence`) and every metric's state (`marketing.metric`)
Where insights land: a post's numbers per day (`post_metric_days`), an account's (`account_metric_days`), and each metric's last state (`metric_sources`)
A post's titles, thumbnails and hooks over time
A file on a post's field: YouTube's thumbnail and subtitles, a Reel's cover, a LinkedIn image or PDF, X's images
The blog from Write

Carousels: one slide set from a video (`draftCarousel` in ./promo.ts), drafted as two posts that share it: a LinkedIn document post (its words plus the slides as a PDF) and an Instagram carousel (a caption plus a square image per slide)
Site chat's store: a visitor's thread by the key their browser holds, their messages and ours, and the Inbox's rows
A post draft checked against its platform's SOP
Client reports: what each report carries and to whom, and every run kept
Client reports: save and list them, work out when each runs, read one period's numbers through `recordsStats`, keep the run, mail each member theirs
The numbers a client report carries: the Marketing Overview's, read the same way (`recordsStats` on the view its tile links to, else the type's first), so the mail and the Overview agree
Content per client: a client's plan, drafts, posts and social reads run on its own logins into its own database
Organic content: posting to each channel, and the plan of what to post
Client social access: a client's own accounts, connected one sign-in each on Wren's apps
The platform reviews Wren's social apps wait on: what each needs, the text to paste, the screencast to record, and live checks of the public pages and callbacks they point at
A client's Google Business Profile as a `ContentChannel`: local posts and reviews through the Business Profile API (v4) on the connected location
SocialAccess: Account → Social

A client's DMs: its Facebook Page's, Instagram's and X's conversations read into its own `reach_contacts` and `reach_messages`, so they land in its Inbox as `dm:<id>` threads; an answer goes back through the same account
Each platform's sign-in: what a token answer means to Wren

Wren's own channels on Account → Social, for the team only: each platform Wren posts to, its handle, how it posts (from config), its token's lapse and last renewal (TokenRenewal's `runs` rows), its last post and last failure (`content_drafts`, `draft_events`), and a Check that runs autobrowse's site check through the same `sites`/`desk` service the channels use: `status` for the site's probe, then that one who-am-I read, then `renew {dry}` for the lapse date
The social accounts a client connects: each platform's app, its sign-in, the scopes it asks, what its review gates and what works before it
The access review log: each step a person or an agent records moves the review's state and is kept
Access reviews: each platform review a client waits on, Wren's own under client `wren`, and every step of it
Client social access: sign-ins in flight and connected accounts
A connected social account as a setup: one step, its token, checked every hour
A client's connected accounts as a `SiteClient`: the same calls Wren's adapters make through autobrowse, sent straight to each platform's official API on the client's token
A connected TikTok's numbers on Account → Social: followers, likes and video count (`user.info.stats`) and its newest videos with their views (`video.list`)
A video's length from its MP4 or QuickTime boxes, read by byte range so the file never sits in memory: walk the top-level boxes to `moov`, then its `mvhd` duration over its timescale
What drafting costs, from the envelope every draft row keeps (`llm.call.usage`): calls and tokens by platform and model over a window
Every draft William finishes, by kind: a post (`content_drafts.text`), a comment's answer (`comments.draft`), a Reddit thread's comment (`reddit_threads.draft`)
A draft's handlers and the input key naming it: what a login limited to a channel may call on a draft it may act on (`calls` in `@wren/core/records`)
The one paid step: an idea in William's words → one draft per platform
A Studio edit beside the film standard
The funnel on a post: video → site → booking
A chapter of a video that is up on YouTube, as a post of its own: the chapter's title and what he said in it (the words the cut keeps, between its start and the next chapter's), with the video's link
A reader's question, answered as a post: the newest `question` comment (as `comments.sort` sorted it) from the last 14 days that no idea came from yet
Auto-reply: what happens when someone writes in, per channel
One Inbox thread as a conversation: the person behind it, every message and touch with them on any channel, our notes, and the channels a reply can take
Reply from the Inbox, with notes and assignees
A reply to mail in a client's connected mailbox: kept in `watch.mail_sent` as `sending` before the provider call, then `sent` or `failed`
A review's reply brief: what Suggest and a draft on arrival write under a review of the business, by its stars
Where a client's DM or comment reply can go: only through the client's own connected account for that platform, never Wren's
A reply from the Inbox: Send or Ask to send, then the channel's own path
A suggested reply for the Inbox's box
An Inbox thread's team state: who has it, open, waiting or closed, snoozed until when
Our posted pieces for learn back: the published drafts an SOP's scope covers, each as the Learn kind it is and with its one real number (`MEASURE_OF`)
What the loop has learned for one platform, read fresh before each draft: the author's recent redraft notes ("shorter", "keep the discord line") and the posts that did best
The Library's Media and SOPs, read only
The media store: an S3 bucket only this repo reads
What a post did, as rows
Our posts for comment drafts (`@wren/core/our-posts`): published or approved, newest first
Posts in the person's own words, stored: an idea and a draft per platform (`./write.ts`)
Pieces: what William makes, each once, with where it went hanging under it
Tomorrow's content plan: each platform's slots against the drafts that hold them, and what is waiting upstream (drafts to review, ideas to draft)
What each platform takes: the length it allows, whether a file is required, and the shape the model is told to write
A platform's playbook (an SOP pushed from the private sops folder) goes into every draft prompt for that platform
Promo posts: one YouTube video → one draft per platform, each in its platform's tone, pointing at the video
The publish queue as rows: approved drafts whose time has come
Posts as console records for the Marketing app: drafts waiting on a person (`marketing_draft_records`) and published ones (`marketing_post_records`)
What follows a post that is up: the row marked, the ledger settled, the first comment, the warm-replies hook
AutoReply: a reply drafted the moment someone writes in, so it waits in To approve before anyone opens the thread
`Blog/wren`: Write's Blog box
Chat: the site bubble's two calls, through the portal Worker, which names the owner from the host
ContentDesk handlers for verdicts: approve, settle, approve a video, pick a thumbnail, reject
The content desk's context, built once per desk: the scope a call drafts in and the drafting steps every group shares
ContentDesk handlers that add, draft, redraft and write posts
ContentDesk handlers that change a draft in place: fields, promotion, funnel, attachments, text
ContentDesk handlers for the formats beyond a post: stories, carousels and slides
ContentDesk handlers that propose a replacement post and settle it
`ContentDesk/default`: the loop's writes that must not run twice
`DraftAsk`: Ask Claude on any draft
InboxDesk: reply from the Inbox on the thread's own channel, ask for a yes when the gate says so, keep notes, assign, close and snooze
KeywordDm: a comment that says a keyword gets the keyword's DM through Meta's private reply, then its public reply when it has one
MailReply: a reply from the Inbox to mail in a client's connected mailbox, sent through that mailbox (Gmail API or Graph), in the same thread
MarketingConsole: a client's Marketing numbers in the portal
`ContentMetrics/default`: looks at each young published post on its tier (`LOOK_TIERS`: every 6 hours at first, then daily, then weekly) through the `Content` service and writes a snapshot row
`Pieces/wren`: Marketing's Today and Pieces read every piece William made, each with its branches
`ContentPlanner/default`: once a day, at `hour` on the fleet's clock, reads tomorrow's plan (slots vs drafts per platform) and says it on Discord
`ClientReport/<id>`: sleeps until the report's next Monday or 1st at 9:00, runs it, sleeps again
`ContentScheduler/default`: publishes approved drafts when they are due
SocialInbox: a client's DMs and comment answers through its own connected accounts
Pushes into the social loops

`SocialWatch/wren`: every 30 minutes, 07:00-23:00 on the fleet's clock, reads comments on our posts of the last 14 days, activity since the newest kept row, and the follower count once a day, through the `Content` service
`VideoDesk`: a video edited from its page
The review seat: a person reads drafts and approves, rejects or edits them
The content loop's tables
A draft as the field editor and the platform preview draw it: its fields with their UI, its words, and a short-lived link for each stored file (thumbnail, cover, the video)
Posts made on the site by hand, read back as published drafts, so `ContentMetrics` reads their numbers like any other post
The slide painter: a chromium draws `slidesHtml`'s page, a 1080 square JPEG per slide (Instagram takes JPEG only) and the whole page as a PDF (one square page each) for LinkedIn
When a platform's posts go out when nobody said: the platform's default slots on the fleet's clock
Ads → Formats: the creative shapes we make ads in
Inbox → Done: what was approved, rejected, edited and sent, from `draft_events`, newest first, with Today and This week as tabs
Comment keywords: a word in a comment on our Instagram or Facebook post sends that person the keyword's DM, through Meta's private reply
A client's Google reviews read off Maps: autobrowse's `web GET /place/reviews`, by the client's Place ID, for a client whose Business Profile isn't reading them through the API

Marketing → Inbox and the Inbox app's "Waiting on you": everything waiting on William's click in one list (`marketing.inbox`): post drafts, comments, DMs, Reddit threads to answer, accepted invites, email replies, text threads and activity
Marketing → Reviews (`marketing.review`, designs/2026-10-09-review-replies.md): every review of the business with its stars and where its reply stands
A 1 or 2 star review rings like an `@` mention: a note on its Inbox thread `@`s the client's owners, and the mention mail tells them once
What SocialWatch keeps: comments on our recent posts as `comments` rows (`channel = content`), activity as `social_activity`, and one follower count per platform per day in `social_days`
`wren status`: is the content week on track? One screen from live tables
Stories (Marketing → Write's Story box): a photo he uploads, or a clip already cut, as a story on Instagram and the Facebook Page at once
Where a Reddit draft posts when nobody named a subreddit: the watched places that take posts, best fit first, less any whose gate holds every account

A picture for each row of a card view (`RecordType.thumbs`): a draft's image, else its poster (thumbnail or cover), else its video; a recording's picked thumbnail, else its first, else a cover, else its preview
Touches from our own accounts' activity, and the whole backfill
The training record's backfill: the drafts made before `draft_events` existed, folded in from where their history sits
Editing a video from its page: Ask Claude's prompt and answer, the page's turns, Undo
The editing agent's pass on one video: the prompt, its answer, writing it, and what the page shows of it: the steps every video run took and the checks he reads before Approve
Marketing → Videos: each `video_edits` row as a record, and Approve
How the posts sound
Posts in the person's own words (Marketing → Write): one draft per platform, no model
A local database for looking at the Inbox: migrated, then the synthetic threads, a note with a mention, an asked reply, and threads assigned to the preview's operator
Synthetic Inbox threads for tests and the local preview

A local database for the libraries' browser pass: the Inbox's synthetic threads (`inbox-preview.ts` runs first), then 600 made-up people at one made-up firm, each with a 555 number and so a profile, so People runs long enough to scroll
A local client for looking at mail replies in its Inbox: a synthetic client with Marketing, two mailboxes (one connected to send, one not), and mail in each

A local database for looking at Outreach: the Inbox's synthetic seed (its LinkedIn DM is a DMs row), plus a second LinkedIn account, an invite waiting on his yes from that account, an accepted one no one has written to yet, and someone else's post with our comment drafted

A local database for looking at Engage's threads: the Inbox's synthetic seed, plus a Reddit thread where one person replied under our comment, then replied to their own reply, and a third person answered them

A local database for looking at touch links: one person with touches that open their item (a Reddit comment, a LinkedIn comment) and touches with no link of their own (our comment, an invite, an Instagram comment whose old url is the numeric media form), all on one profile
